I had put up with a thousand small injuries from Fortunato, but when he dared to insult me, I made a promise of revenge. <break time="0.8s" /> You, who know my nature so well, will understand that I never said a single word of threat out loud. <break time="0.8s" /> I would have my revenge in the end, but it had to be done in a way that brought no risk to me. <break time="0.8s" /> A wrong is not paid back if the avenger is punished in return, or if the wrongdoer never learns who is punishing him. <break time="0.8s" /> So I did nothing, either in words or in actions, that made Fortunato doubt my good will toward him. <break time="0.8s" /> I kept smiling in his face, and he did not notice that my smile now came from the thought of his ruin. <break time="0.8s" /> Fortunato, a man respected and even feared in many ways, had one weak point, his pride in his knowledge of wine. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening during the wild days of the carnival season, I met my friend in the crowded streets at dusk. <break time="0.8s" /> He had been drinking a great deal, and he was dressed as a clown, with a striped suit and a pointed cap with bells. <break time="0.8s" /> I was so pleased to see him that I thought I would never stop shaking his hand.
